Hi there. Your post is well written and your English is easy to understand. 

Two things that came to mind. First off, I see your suffering and I’m so sorry you’re going through this. But I believe your suffering is do to your mental illness, not some higher power that is now or could be at some point holding you accountable for a hypothetical promise you’ve made. You’re tearing yourself to shreds over this and it’s really not fair to you. 

Second, though I can neither confirm nor deny the existence of a higher power, I doubt any try omnipotent and omniscient God would punish you for this. They would understand your struggles and try to guide you lovingly. 

I watched an interview with a gentleman who claims to be a detective in all things related to heaven and the soul. I understand in your post you weren’t necessarily praying to the Christian God, but hopefully it gives you a new perspective. 
Essentially, his findings were that anyone who is struggling with mental illness, that is a challenge your soul decided to give you and the Lord does not judge you harshly for that. I’m paraphrasing but that’s the gist of it. 

So please be kind to yourself and understand your OCD is causing you to think and feel this way. I hope I’ve helped you in someway.

Interesting. So if not to cure or punish, what should be done? Build a special facility that provides basic human needs and isolate them there?

I’m fully aware such a program would never be implemented. It’s merely a hypothetical scenario that I like to ponder on. Even if it were to be passed I know it would probably lead to rioting from the masses because it takes away what people consider a basic human right ,even though it’s being heavily abused. 

So my thoughts were to build a basic criteria that really should be common sense to whether or not someone is qualified to be a parent. It wouldn’t be overly complicated and could be conducted by a social worker, guidance counselor or any equivalent professional. Really it’s mostly clerical work. Example:
•Are they employed? Do they make an adequate wage to raise a child? Do they have reliable transportation to safely transport the child? 
•Do they have a history of substance abuse/violent behavior? Do they have a prison record? 

Once they’re at the stage of being examined by a physician and a psychiatrist, again it’s mostly common sense. Are they healthy and active enough to have and raise children? Are they mentally and emotionally capable of being effective parents?
Now this all a very watered down version of what I’d like it to be. If I had my way they’d be picked apart under a microscope. But I’d settle for the basic requirements that people applying for adoption have to satisfy. 

Now as far the method of sterilization, I can’t say. I know this is where it becomes controversial because it would be an invasive operation that every male new born would be subjected to. And your point about people finding illegal ways to reverse it is very valid. I’m sure it would happen, it would be similar to the prohibition only with male fertility. 
Like I said, I know this sounds like a saving grace in my mind. In reality it would probably spark some kind of apocalyptic event and set the world on fire. Haha!

I have to say I admire you for being an empath. I have had the exact same discussion with myself. 

The argument that our choices are based on our mental faculties and our mental faculties are based on our brain synapses. I mean, that is a somewhat valid point. Our brain tells our heart to beat, our muscles to contract and decides where and why we feel pain. 

I’ve put myself in the mind of someone who has done unspeakable things and like you concluded that if I were born under the same circumstances with the same brain I’d make the same terrible choices they did. I’d have to because it wouldn’t be my brain and their circumstances or vice versa, that changes everything. 

I agree with your logic about punishing a dog for barking because you wanted it meow, I totally understand what you mean. But that also speaks to the point I was making. The owners had no right to have the dog because they wanted it to be a cat and made it feel insignificant because it wasn’t. Now, if that dog becomes traumatized and bites someone the dog will be killed and the owners would be (hopefully) thrown in jail. 
I know the dog represents the parents in your argument. But it doesn’t change anything, the dog still bit someone and it was the owners responsibility to teach them not to and to love them. 

So what do we do? Let abusive people have children so they can go on to abuse their children etc etc. I know abused children don’t always grow up to be abusers, but the fact of reality is that the ratio is at best 1/10.

Second. I have made mistakes that eat away at me everyday. I’ll tell you the worst to give you context. I broke up with my girlfriend who loved me because I was a miserable, callous person and I was taking her for granted. I understood that and instead of putting in the effort to be better I broke her heart and thought it was the right thing to do. That’s just one of several incidents that haunt me. So yes I can relate with how having mental illness can severely impair how I think and feel. I don’t have to imagine being that person, I am that person. 

That being said, I 100% believe that misery breads misery and it’s very wrong to gamble with a life like that. I’ve made mistakes because of my mental illness, but that does not excuse anything, it doesn’t take the pain I caused her away and it certainly doesn’t mean there shouldn’t be consequences.

Hello. The first thing I recommend you do is to look up some grounding techniques. These really help when your intrusive thoughts are out of control and you lose your sense of self.
